chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi from Muhammad ibn Musaddif who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Prostration is indeed upon the forehead, and not upon the nose.'

key_terms.السُّجُودُ: Prostration (the act of bowing down in prayer)

ai.seo_question: Where exactly should the forehead be placed during prostration in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise anatomical requirement for valid prostration, distinguishing the forehead (jibhah) from the nose to ensure the forehead touches the ground directly. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on literal adherence to the Prophet’s description of sujood, reinforcing the physical integrity of the prayer posture as a sign of humility before God.
